rationale:
Final design: kd 0.8, with every other value as in the raced iteration-5 design. The critique is partly accepted and the one-factor test is kept.

Evidence. The raced iteration-5 design (kd 0.6) scored 356.57, the best so far. Holding geometry, base_speed, kp, ki and line_loss fixed while kd moved 0.2 to 0.4 to 0.6 gave scores of 52.11, 220.09 and 356.57. Oval finish rate rose 0, 30, 85 percent. Between kd 0.4 and 0.6, oval steering oscillation fell slightly (0.265 to 0.253) and control effort fell (7.6 to 5.7). The critique is right that the gain is diminishing (+168, then +136), so extrapolating to 0.8 does not establish a further rise.

Accepted from the critique: (a) Per-track acceptance is needed. Slalom progress fell from 0.173 at kd 0.4 to 0.120 at kd 0.6, so a higher total score could hide a slalom loss. (b) The oscillation risk should be stated from the data: the rise was sharp from 0.2 to 0.4 and has plateaued or fallen since. (c) Noise bound: at the assumed signal-rate noise of about 2 units/s, kd 0.8 gives about 1.6 turn, about 560 PWM. This is an assumption, not a measurement, and it is below base PWM of about 3276. (d) The non-oval tracks still end at max_error of about 0.065 m with one line-loss event each, and kd alone does not address that mechanism. I do not claim kd fixes those tracks.

Rejected from the critique: I do not switch line_loss mode or change kp, ki or geometry in this race. Those are separate factors and would break the one-factor test. Line-loss recovery is the next candidate if kd 0.8 does not help the non-oval tracks.

Decision rule (per track, not total score alone). Accept kd 0.8 as the new base only if all three hold: oval finish rate is at least 85 percent with oval mean score at least 863; s-bend progress is above 0.379; slalom progress is at least 0.12. If the total rises but slalom progress falls below 0.12, treat the result as mixed and keep kd 0.6 as the base. If oval finish rate falls below 85 percent or oscillation rises enough to hurt the oval, kd 0.6 is the ceiling and the next single-variable test is line-loss recovery.

Expected results (hypotheses, not data): oval finish rate holds at or above 85 percent; s-bend progress is at or above about 0.38; slalom progress is at or above 0.12. A flat result is plausible and would not clearly separate kd 0.6 from 0.8 within seed noise. Completion on s-bend and slalom remains unlikely at this speed.
